title: IceCreamClear
question: How is ice cream made?
hook: A scoop of ice cream is half air. The rest is millions of ice crystals, tiny balls of fat and a syrup that never freezes. Pull a scoop apart, chill a pot with salt and ice, spin the scraper blades, whip in the air, design your own scoop, and see why kulfi melts slowly and a thawed tub turns icy.

explainer.title: A scoop is four things at once
explainer.text: Under a microscope, ice cream is ice crystals about 50 micrometres across, air bubbles a little bigger, fat globules about 1 micrometre across, and a thick sugar syrup that is still liquid. By volume a typical scoop is about half air, a quarter to a third ice, a twentieth fat, and the rest syrup.

explainer.title: Salt makes ice colder than ice
explainer.text: Sweet mix only starts to freeze at about −2.6 °C, so plain ice at 0 °C can never freeze it. Salt makes the ice melt, and melting takes heat from the pot itself. Ice and salt can reach −21 °C. That is how a hand-cranked pot and a kulfi matka work.

explainer.title: Freeze fast and scrape the wall
explainer.text: Big crystals feel icy: the tongue notices them above about 50 micrometres. A freezer barrel chilled to about −30 °C starts crystals quickly, and spinning blades scrape them off the wall as tiny seeds. The ice cream leaves at about −5 °C with half its water frozen, then is hardened in a blast freezer.

explainer.title: Half of it is air
explainer.text: The dasher whips air in as it scrapes. Overrun is the extra volume: at 100% the mix has doubled, so half of every scoop is air. Clumps of part-solid milk fat brace each bubble. In India, FSSAI requires a litre of ice cream to weigh at least 525 grams, which caps the air.

explainer.title: Sugar is the antifreeze
explainer.text: Sugar lowers the freezing point, and as ice forms the syrup left behind gets stronger. So the water never all freezes: about a quarter is still liquid at −14 °C. That is why a spoon goes in. Sugar, fat, air and serving temperature together decide how firm, smooth and long-lasting a scoop is.

explainer.title: Kulfi, gelato and the refreeze problem
explainer.text: Kulfi is thick, slow-boiled milk frozen without churning, so it holds almost no air and melts slowly. Gelato has less fat and air, and soft serve is never hardened. A product made with vegetable fat must be labelled frozen dessert. Each time a tub warms up, its small crystals melt and the big ones grow, so it turns icy.

concepts.def: The air whipped into ice cream, given as extra volume. 100% overrun means the mix doubled in volume.
Dissolved sugar or salt lowers the temperature at which water freezes.
The lowest freezing point of a salt and water mixture: −21.1 °C at 23.3% common salt.
A chilled barrel whose blades shave ice off the wall as fast as it forms, while a dasher whips in air.
Part-solid fat globules sticking together in clumps without merging. The clumps hold the air bubbles.
As ice forms, the sugar is left in less water, so the remaining syrup gets ever harder to freeze.
Small ice crystals vanishing and large ones growing during storage, which makes old ice cream icy.
Slow-reduced, sweetened milk frozen in moulds without churning. Dense, with almost no air.
Under FSSAI rules, a product like ice cream made with vegetable fat instead of milk fat. It must be labelled as such.
